text: First of all, then, I urge that petitions, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for all people—
for kings and all who hold authority, so that we may lead a quiet and peaceful life in all godliness and dignity.
This is good and pleasing in the sight of God our Savior,
who wants all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.
For there is one God, and one mediator between God and humanity, the man Christ Jesus,
who gave himself as a ransom for all—the testimony given at the proper time.
For this I was appointed a herald and an apostle—I am telling the truth, I am not lying—a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth.
So I want the men everywhere to pray, lifting up holy hands without anger or argument.
Likewise, I want the women to adorn themselves with decent clothing, with modesty and self-control, not with elaborate hairstyles or gold or pearls or expensive garments,
but with good works, as befits women who profess to worship God.
A woman should learn quietly, in full submission.
I do not permit a woman to teach or to have authority over a man; she is to remain quiet.
For Adam was formed first, then Eve;
and Adam was not the one deceived; it was the woman who was thoroughly deceived and became a transgressor.

versions.text: and Adam was not deceived, but the woman was deceived and fell into transgression.
versions.explanation: The Greek uses two different verbs (ἠπατήθη, then the intensified ἐξαπατηθεῖσα), which the current rendering flattens into the same word twice. Also, ἐν παραβάσει γέγονεν is literally 'came to be in transgression' — i.e. 'became a transgressor' — which is slightly stronger and clearer than 'fell into transgression.'

text: Yet she will be saved through childbearing—if they continue in faith and love and holiness, with self-control. [Footnote: The Greek is difficult; it may also be understood as 'kept safe through childbirth' or 'saved through the birth of the Child.']

versions.text: Yet she will be saved through childbearing—if they continue in faith and love and holiness, with self-control.
versions.explanation: This verse is notoriously ambiguous, and 'saved through childbearing' read aloud without any note could easily be heard as teaching that salvation comes by bearing children. A brief footnote noting the alternative readings guards against that misunderstanding without altering the text.
